0.0.n: An elevated, old-fashioned possessive expression, fitting a formal declaration of loyalty.

0.1.n: Refers to the person the speaker serves.

0.3.n: The family name of the speaker’s master.

0.4.n: The given name of the speaker’s master.

0.5.n: Marks the person represented in the expression に代わって.

0.6.n: The て-form of 代わる links this representative role to the action in the next line.

1.0.n: Before the speaker’s own name, この adds emphasis, like declaring I myself.

1.2.n: This character begins the given name 琴鳴; it is not a separate word here.

1.3.n: This character completes the name 琴鳴; it is not a form of the verb 鳴る here.

1.4.n: Marks the named speaker as the person accepting the challenge.

1.5.n: This character begins the family name 司波; it is not a separate word here.

1.6.n: This character completes the family name 司波; it does not mean wave here.

1.7.n: 達也 is a given name; 殿 is a formal honorific showing respect.

1.8.n: Connects Tatsuya’s name to the challenge he issued.

1.9.n: Names what the speaker formally agrees to accept.

1.10.n: Marks 挑戦 as the thing being accepted.

1.11.n: The stem of 受ける with お begins the humble expression お受けします.

1.12.n: The polite form of する completes お受けします, respectfully announcing the speaker’s acceptance.

2.0.n: This character begins the given name 琴鳴, used here to address her directly.

2.1.n: This character completes the name 琴鳴; it is not the verb 鳴る here.

3.0.n: A given name used to address the listener directly.

3.1.n: Adds ordinary polite respect to Katsushige’s name.

3.3.n: Refers to the proposed arrangement or resolution.

3.4.n: Marks これ as the topic being evaluated.

3.5.n: An adjective expressing that this resolution is favorable.

3.6.n: Refers to settling the dispute, rather than simply any result.

4.0.n: Refers to the result of the challenge.

4.1.n: Marks 結果 as what may turn out in different ways.

4.2.n: Works with なろうと to cover any possible outcome.

4.3.n: The volitional form of なる expresses a hypothetical possibility here, not someone’s intention.

4.4.n: After なろう, と makes the clause mean regardless of how things turn out.

4.6.n: Combines with 候補 to specify the leadership position at stake.

4.7.n: Together with 当主, this identifies someone eligible to become the family head.

4.8.n: Marks the candidate as the person who would be harmed or lost.

4.9.n: Describes someone suffering harm; it does not mean injuring another person.

4.10.n: Turns 傷つく into an event that can be discussed as a thing.

4.11.n: The first も pairs with the second under ない to rule out both events.

4.12.n: The passive form of 失う presents the candidate as someone who might be lost.

4.13.n: Turns 失われる into an event, parallel to 傷つくこと.

4.14.n: Pairs with the earlier も; the final negative makes the combination neither event nor the other.

4.15.n: Negates both listed possibilities: injury and loss.

4.16.n: Adds an explanatory tone before the polite ending です.

4.17.n: Keeps the explanation polite after ないの.

4.18.n: Presents this lack of danger as the reason the resolution is desirable.

5.0.n: Rejects a conclusion drawn from the previous statement: that fact alone does not justify what follows.

5.2.n: A familiar, blunt pronoun that can signal closeness or authority; here it carries strong emotion.

5.3.n: Marks the listener as the person the speaker might lose.

5.4.n: The て-form of 失う connects to もいい to describe something supposedly acceptable.

5.5.n: After the て-form, も combines with いい to express permission or acceptability.

5.6.n: Completes 失ってもいい, the idea that losing the listener would be permissible.

5.7.n: Introduces the preceding statement as the content of こと.

5.8.n: Packages the preceding idea as a conclusion that the speaker rejects.

5.9.n: Marks the resulting conclusion in ことになる, meaning that something follows or amounts to something.

5.10.n: Emphasizes that this particular conclusion does not follow.

5.11.n: The negative form of なる completes the forceful rejection of that conclusion.

0.lit: On behalf of my master, Shibata Katsushige,
0.tip: Person + に代わって means acting on that person’s behalf.

1.lit: This Tsutsumi Kotona humbly accepts Lord Shiba Tatsuya’s challenge.
1.tip: お + verb stem + します respectfully lowers the speaker’s own action.

2.tip: 琴鳴 is one given name, even though the subtitle tokenizer split it into two pieces.

3.lit: Katsushige-san, as for this, it is a desirable resolution.
3.tip: は marks what the speaker is commenting on: here, the proposed resolution.

4.lit: Because, however the outcome may turn out, the family-head candidate will neither suffer injury nor be lost.
4.tip: Two clauses ending in ことも followed by ない rule out both possibilities.

5.lit: Even so, it does not follow that losing you is acceptable!
5.tip: だからといって signals that the previous fact does not justify the conclusion being rejected.
